html.body: REM1499455565,6124352017-05-022017-05-05REM DOCUMENTApplication No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000REMARKSApplicant submits this Reply in response to the Office Action mailed on February 2, 2017.Status of the ClaimsClaims 1-20 are currently pending in this application. By this Amendment, Applicant amends claims 1, 7-9, and 15-17. The originally filed specification and drawings fully support the subject matter of the amended claims, for example, at paragraph [029] and [035]. Applicant believes that this Amendment adds no new matter.Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the pending rejections for at least the reasons that follow.Examiner's InterviewApplicant sincerely appreciates the courtesies that Examiner Alter andSupervisory Examiner Kahelin extended to Applicant's representatives, Dr. Leo Grady, Chris Agrawal, and Lian Huang, during the Examiner's Interview conducted on January 12, 2017.During the interview, the parties discussed the Section 112 Rejections, as well as the differences between the cited Taylor and Mabotuwana references and the claims as filed in the amendment filed December 21, 2016. Examiner Alter agreed to withdraw the Section 112 Rejections, and indicated that further search and consideration would be necessary for the prior art rejections. If the Examiner believes that any additional issues should be addressed to expedite the allowance of this application, Applicant invites the Examiner to contact the undersigned to expedite those issues.-10-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000Section 112 RejectionsClaims 1-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) (pre-AIA) (secondparagraph) as allegedly being indefinite in reciting "viscera or bowel." To expedite prosecution, Applicant amends the claims to render the Section 112 rejections moot. Applicant thus requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 112 rejections.Section 103 RejectionsApplicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1-20, which were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Taylor (U.S. Publication No. 2012/0041318 Al) ("Taylor') in view of T. Mabotuwana, L. Cheng, and A. Pullan, ("A model of blood flow in the mesenteric arterial system" Biomed Eng Online. 2007) ("Mabotuwana").The Office Action interprets "blood flow demand" as referring to, "baseline(resting) mean blood flow." (Office Action, page 5.) To further clarify the claims and distinguish the claim features from cited references, Applicant amends the claims to recite, "determining a blood flow demand of the portion of the patient's bowel based on the determined mass, wherein the blood flow demand varies based on the patient's physiological state." Neither Taylor nor Mabotuwana, individually or in combination, would have rendered obvious the above-recited subject matter.For the reasons discussed, Applicant submits that claims 1-20 are allowable over all of the cited references. Accordingly, Applicant requests the Examiner's reconsideration and withdrawal of the Section 103 rejections.-11-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000Double Patenting RejectionsIn the Office Action, claims 1-20 were provisionally rejected based onnonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 21-40 of copending divisional U.S. Application No. 15/080,829. Without conceding to the assertions in the double patenting rejections, Applicant requests that the Examiner hold the double patenting rejections in abeyance until such time as no other issues remain in the application, and the pending claims are deemed otherwise allowable. At that time, Applicant will investigate the need for any terminal disclaimers.ConclusionThe Office Action contains characterization of the claims and the related art with which the Applicant does not necessarily agree. Unless expressly noted otherwise, Applicant declines to subscribe to any statement or characterization in the Office Action.In discussing the specification, claims, and drawings in this Reply, it is to beunderstood that Applicant is in no way intending to limit the scope of the claims to any exemplary embodiments described in the specification or abstract and/or shown in the drawings. Rather, Applicant is entitled to have the claims interpreted broadly to the maximum extent permitted by statute, regulation, and applicable case law.In view of the foregoing remarks, Applicant submits that this claimed invention is neither anticipated nor rendered obvious in view of the prior art references cited against this application. Applicant therefore requests the reconsideration and reexamination of the application, and the timely allowance of the pending claims.If the Examiner believes a telephone conversation might advance prosecution, the Examiner is invited to call applicant's undersigned representative at 202-803-8075.-12-Application No.: 14/994,555Attorney Docket No.: 11541-0039-01000Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account No. 50-5906. In addition, the Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any additional fees due and any other fees due under 37 C.F.R. § 1.16 or § 1.17 during the pendency of this application to Deposit Account No. 50-5906.Respectfully submitted, BOOKOFF McANDREWS, PLLCCustomer Number: 108,449Dated: May 2, 2017 By: SVG14994555.05-02-2017.J2AH7P9ZPXXIFW1.REM.4.11.1272.1483.2210.1529.svg0.1533.127Chemistry Lian HuangReg.
